anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet the USB-C receptacle J1 VBUS pin (A4) is wired to a global label named 'VBUS'. The same name 'VBUS' appears on the power sheet as the output of the power mux U7 (TPS2121RUXR, pin 1 OUT) and as the input of the buck converter U4 (AP63203WU, pin 3 IN). The mux's USB input pin 2 (IN2) instead carries the global label '+5V', which has no connection from the USB connector.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec, the USB connector's VBUS pin must sit on the '+5V' net that feeds U7.IN2, and the internal pre-buck rail named 'VBUS' is downstream of the mux and must remain distinct from the USB 5V net.

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch (sheet 1/4 & 2/4): J1 pin A4 -> 'VBUS'; power.kicad_sch (sheet 3/4): U7 pin 1 OUT -> 'VBUS', U7 pin 2 IN2 -> '+5V', U4 pin 3 IN -> 'VBUS'
J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2 (IN2) ... note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.

anomalies.impact: USB 5V is tied directly to the mux output / buck input rather than to the mux's IN2 input. The power mux can no longer arbitrate the USB supply (IN2 floats); when the barrel jack is also present the mux drives VBUS to 12V while USB forces 5V onto the same node, causing back-feed/contention and defeating the seamless-switchover design.

anomalies.observed: On the thermocouple sheet the shared SCK line of all three MAX31855 chips (pin 5) is net NET0019, and the three CS lines are NET0018/NET0008/NET0006. On the MCU sheet NET0019 lands on the GPIO04 pin, NET0018 on GPIO03, NET0008 on GPIO05, NET0006 on GPIO07 (and GPIO06/NET0009 is used for the WS2812 DIN).
anomalies.expected: The spec (confirmed from firmware) maps SCK to GPIO5 and the three thermocouple CS lines to GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7.

evidence.quote: thermocouples.kicad_sch: U1.5 SCK = NET0019; mcu.kicad_sch: NET0019 on GPIO04, NET0008 on GPIO05, NET0009 on GPIO06
SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7 ... sck on GPIO5 ... three independent CS Output pins on GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7

anomalies.impact: The SPI clock and chip-select signals are on different GPIOs than the firmware expects (SCK on GPIO4 instead of GPIO5, a CS on GPIO5 instead of GPIO6, and GPIO6 repurposed for the status LED). Sequential thermocouple polling would select the wrong device / clock the wrong line, so temperature reads would fail.

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the intended design: most clearly, the USB-C VBUS pin is wired to the internal 'VBUS' net (mux output / buck input) instead of the '+5V' mux-input net, bypassing the power mux; additionally the thermocouple SPI SCK/CS nets appear mapped to GPIOs that conflict with the firmware's GPIO5-SCK / GPIO4-6-7-CS assignment.
